subject.title: build(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Do the workflow/security owners accept the fourteen upstream GitHub Action revisions, including the token-, publishing-, attestation-, and Codex-facing actions, for OpenClaw’s privileged workflows?
rationale: This is an intentional third-party code execution and credential-boundary change; neither a mechanical review nor passing unit-style checks can establish the repository’s acceptable supply-chain trust decision.

options.title: Accept after release verification
options.body: Verify the pinned SHAs against the intended upstream releases and accept the updates after the refreshed branch completes required workflow checks.

options.title: Split high-privilege updates
options.body: Keep lower-risk setup and labeling action bumps separate while reviewing token, release, Docker publishing, attestation, and Codex action upgrades individually.

options.title: Hold selected revisions
options.body: Pause the PR and retain current pins for any upstream action whose release changes are not acceptable for privileged workflows.

recommendation.title: Accept after release verification
recommendation.body: Verify the pinned SHAs against the intended upstream releases and accept the updates after the refreshed branch completes required workflow checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available routing candidate for the repository-level workflow/security acceptance decision; narrower ownership could not be established from the available read-only evidence.
